app/vite.config.ts:1 — defineConfig + configureServer middleware, the current plugin API, unchanged in Vite 8

latest_apis.rationale: Everything used is the current generation: Vite 8 config/plugin API, TS 5.9 strict, ESM throughout. Nothing deprecated or legacy-era; it just doesn't lean on any of the newer conveniences (e.g. `define` for env injection) that would be nice-to-have.

app/src/components.ts:27 — img loading="lazy" with width/height to avoid layout shift
app/src/style.css:41 — :focus-visible; tokens.css via CSS custom properties

app/src/pages/home.ts:139-144 — hand-rolled setTimeout debounce (no platform alternative exists; acceptable)
app/src/api.ts:41 — fetch without AbortController signal; stale requests are only neutralized by the render token (main.ts:14)
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform consistently (fetch, URL APIs, streams, lazy images, focus-visible), keeping runtime deps at zero. A signal/AbortController story for in-flight fetches is the one gap.

evidence: app/package.json:10-13 — only typescript ^5.9.3 and vite ^8.3.5, both devDependencies; zero runtime deps
app/src/util.ts:1-3 — hand-rolled esc() instead of pulling a template/escape library
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: nothing shipped to production beyond the app's own bundle, and the two dev tools are the current stable majors.

evidence: app/src/api.ts + app/src/data.ts — all HTTP access funneled through two modules; pages consume typed shapes (SpeciesRef, TypeInfo in data.ts:5-13)
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:251-271 — sorting reconstructs MoveRow data by scraping rendered cell text and hrefs, so a markup change silently breaks sorting
app/src/data.ts:31 — (d.results as any[]) and untyped `any` API records throughout data.ts and pages/pokemon.ts:44 weaken the otherwise-strict boundary
app/vite.config.ts:6-18 vs app/server.mjs:32-36 — /config.js generation duplicated in the dev plugin and the prod server
app/src/pages/home.ts:122-125 — direct history.pushState/replaceState instead of reusing navigate() from nav.ts:8
app/src/components.ts:16 — module-level sectionCounter for unique heading ids keeps mutating across renders
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access and rendering are well isolated, so most requirement changes stay local. But the DOM-scraping sorter, pervasive `any` at the API boundary, and duplicated nav/config plumbing are exactly the things that make the next change cost more than it should.

findings.issue: Table sorting derives row state from rendered DOM (cell textContent and href scraping), coupling behavior to markup; any presentational change to moveRowHtml breaks sorting silently.
findings.suggestion: Keep the MoveRow[] data in a closure (or on the table via a WeakMap) and render from it, so sorting and rendering share one source of truth.

findings.issue: API responses are typed as any at the boundary (data.ts:31,53; pages/pokemon.ts:44,87; pages/move.ts:8) despite strict mode, so shape drift from the API surfaces as runtime breakage not type errors.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the consumed API records (species, pokemon, move, type) in api.ts/data.ts and validate or cast at the boundary only.

findings.issue: Fetches are not abortable; navigation away from a heavy page (e.g. the moves section fires one /move/ request per move, pages/pokemon.ts:173-175) leaves stale requests running, with correctness guaranteed only by the render token in main.ts:14.
findings.suggestion: Thread an AbortController signal through apiJson per navigation and abort on route change.

findings.issue: The /config.js endpoint is implemented twice — in the dev plugin and again in server.mjs:32-36 — so a change to the runtime config contract must be made in two places.
findings.suggestion: Factor the config-snippet generation into one shared module imported by both, or move to Vite's `define`/`import.meta.env` if build-time embedding ever becomes acceptable.

findings.issue: home.ts manipulates history directly, duplicating nav.ts's navigate() (nav.ts:8-12) instead of reusing it.
findings.suggestion: Reuse navigate() from nav.ts for filter changes so history/navigation logic lives in one module.

findings.issue: Module-level sectionCounter for unique heading ids is shared mutable state that survives across page renders.
findings.suggestion: Derive the id from the (already unique per page) section title plus an explicit index passed by the caller, or reset per render.

summary: A lean, current-generation vanilla TS + Vite 8 app: zero runtime dependencies, platform-first choices, and all HTTP access isolated behind two small modules. The main aging risks are behavioral — DOM-scraped table sorting and untyped API records — plus small duplicated config/navigation plumbing. Solid as a PR; the two medium findings are worth fixing before this becomes the codebase others copy patterns from.

apis.replacement: Navigation API is still experimental; History API remains the current way
Confirmed current in Vite 8 (vite.dev plugin API docs; Vite 8 changed the bundler, not the plugin API)
